name: Minocycline
route_note: Oral capsules or extended-release tablets; IV formulation; topical foam for acne; periodontal microspheres.
targets: 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit (aminoacyl-tRNA A site)

discovery.note: A lipophilic semi-synthetic tetracycline with a dimethylamino substituent, giving good tissue and CNS penetration. Year is the first patent filing.

tagline: Lipophilic tetracycline used for acne, MRSA and Acinetobacter infections
summary: Minocycline is a highly lipophilic semi-synthetic tetracycline developed by Lederle. It is widely used for acne and also retains activity against some MRSA and Acinetobacter baumannii strains, but it has a distinctive profile of vestibular, pigmentary and autoimmune adverse effects.
mechanism: Minocycline binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and prevents aminoacyl-tRNA from binding the A site, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis (bacteriostatic).

Its high lipophilicity gives excellent tissue and CNS penetration and it is less affected by some tetracycline efflux pumps (e.g. TetK), preserving activity against some resistant staphylococci and Acinetobacter. It also has anti-inflammatory effects relevant to acne.
uses: Inflammatory acne vulgaris (oral and topical foam)
Skin and soft-tissue infections including some MRSA
Meningococcal carriage (historical), nocardiosis and leprosy (alternative regimens)

history.title: Aureomycin
history.detail: Lederle reports chlortetracycline (Aureomycin), the first tetracycline.

history.title: Doxycycline
history.detail: Pfizer's doxycycline is introduced, a contemporary semi-synthetic tetracycline.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: Minocin is approved in the US.

history.title: Arestin
history.detail: Minocycline microspheres (Arestin) are approved for periodontitis.

history.title: Extended-release acne product
history.detail: Solodyn, an extended-release formulation for acne, is approved in the US.

history.title: Topical foam
history.detail: The FDA approves Amzeeq, the first topical minocycline, for acne.

serious: Blue-grey hyperpigmentation of skin, teeth and other tissues

facts: Long-term minocycline can cause blue-black pigmentation of skin, nails, teeth, bone and even the thyroid gland ('black thyroid').
